bls-census.name: bls-census
bls-census.description: Free labor-force, demographic, and earnings panels from the BLS public data API (LFPR, employment, payrolls, CPI/PPI — no key needed), Census ACS5 / basic-monthly CPS (county demographics and CPS person extracts — free key required), and SSA OACT period life tables. Zero overlap with WRDS/CRSP. Use for shift-share / Bartik instruments (cohort aging, local labor demand, retirement-channel shifters), labor-finance, household-finance, and macro-cross-section work.

claude.argument-hint: [BLS series ID, ACS variable, or description]

call-reports.name: call-reports
call-reports.description: Quarterly bank balance sheets / income statements without WRDS's bank library or S&P CIQ. Three free no-key sources, each with a different ID: (1) FFIEC CDR bulk SDF — literal RCON/RIAD-coded Call Reports for every FDIC-insured bank, keyed by IDRSSD, scraped from the ASP.NET bulk-download form (the documented free path, brittle by design); (2) FR Y-9C BHCF flat files — consolidated bank-holding-company statements, BHCK-coded, keyed by RSSD9001 (Chicago Fed 1986Q1-2021Q1 live, NIC user-placed for 2021Q2+); (3) FDIC Financial Data API — robust standardized (non-RCON) panel keyed by CERT, the reliable fallback and the RSSD<->CERT crosswalk. Use for the banking / monetary-transmission / intermediary-asset-pricing channel: bank lending, deposits, liquidity regulation, CET1 capital, NIM.

claude.argument-hint: [quarter e.g. 2023Q4, RSSD/CERT id, or RCON code]

canonical-packages.name: canonical-packages
canonical-packages.description: Policy + procedure for not reimplementing econometric methods that have canonical, author-maintained packages. Field-tier finance referees (JF/JFE/RFS) reject custom code that re-derives well-known estimators (HonestDiD, Sensemakr, Callaway-Sant'Anna, wild cluster bootstrap, etc.) — see GitHub issue #36. This skill does NOT catalog packages; it tells you when to look one up (before writing code for any named econometric method), where to look (method author's site, PyPI, CRAN, Stata SSC, WebSearch), and how to document a legitimate deviation via the (a)–(d) justification taxonomy. The actual canonical-package discovery is done on demand by the empiricist (before coding) and by the `method-checker` agent (during audit at Stage 3a step 7.5) using PyPI / CRAN / SSC queries plus training knowledge.

chen-zimmerman.name: chen-zimmerman
chen-zimmerman.description: Open Source Asset Pricing dataset (Chen & Zimmerman 2022). 212 firm-level anomaly signals with portfolio returns. Use for cross-sectional calibration, testing anomaly predictions, and constructing characteristic-sorted portfolios.

edgar.name: edgar
edgar.description: Access SEC EDGAR filings, financial statements, and full-text search. Use for corporate finance research — 10-K/10-Q analysis, governance, disclosure, insider trading, institutional holdings.

flex-mining.name: flex-mining
flex-mining.description: Flexible data mining strategies from Chen, Lopez-Lira & Zimmermann. 30,000+ long-short trading strategies from CRSP/Compustat ratios. Use for benchmarking published predictors against data-mined alternatives, testing sufficiency of published literature, and studying the cross-section of expected returns.

form-5500.name: form-5500
form-5500.description: DOL EBSA Form 5500 — annual ERISA filings for every U.S. pension/welfare plan with ≥100 participants. Schedule H gives plan-level asset breakdowns including mutual-fund holdings (INT_REG_INVST_CO_*_AMT); Schedule R covers retirement-plan distributions and rollovers. Free public-use research files. Use for retirement, household finance, defined-contribution/401(k), and labor-finance research.

fred.name: fred
fred.description: Fetch macroeconomic and financial time series from FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data). Use when calibrating models to macro moments, testing time-series predictions, or getting risk-free rates, spreads, and macro indicators.

hrs-scf.name: hrs-scf
hrs-scf.description: Household-survey panels for retirement, wealth, and household balance sheets. SCF (Survey of Consumer Finances, Federal Reserve, triennial 1989–2022) downloads with NO key — Summary Extract and Full Public Data Set with 5 multiply-imputed implicates. HRS (Health & Retirement Study / RAND HRS Longitudinal File) is registration-walled: the helper reads a user-placed extract from data/hrs_scf/hrs/ (the realistic workflow — bulk download after accepting the data-use agreement) and documents the registration step; it never fails silently. Use for retirement timing, IRA/401(k) balances by cohort, wealth distribution, and household-finance micro-validation (e.g. pairing HRS individual retirement timing with macro Bartik shifters). Rollover/pension-disposition events need HRS detailed-pension stems supplied via stems= (documented, not the default panel).

claude.argument-hint: [SCF year, RAND HRS variable, or description]

ken-french.name: ken-french
ken-french.description: Download factor returns, portfolio returns, and breakpoints from the Ken French Data Library. Use for asset pricing calibration, computing alphas, and building test assets.

mutual-funds.name: mutual-funds
mutual-funds.description: CRSP Mutual Fund Database + Thomson Reuters holdings via WRDS. Fund returns, NAV, TNA, fees, flows, holdings, and style classifications. Use for mutual fund performance, flow-performance, holdings-based analysis, and fund manager skill.

sec-funds.name: sec-funds
sec-funds.description: Parse SEC fund-specific filings from EDGAR — N-CEN (annual census: advisers, underwriters, securities lending, expense waivers), NPORT-P (monthly portfolio holdings), and N-1A/485BPOS Risk/Return XBRL (per-share-class fee tables: management fee, 12b-1, gross/net expense ratio). Free path to mutual-fund fees/holdings without CRSP. Use for mutual-fund fee, retirement/DC-channel, and holdings-based research.

wrds.name: wrds
wrds.description: Query WRDS (Wharton Research Data Services) for CRSP, Compustat, IBES, options, insider trading, and other financial databases. Use for firm-level stock returns, accounting data, analyst forecasts, and cross-sectional/panel analysis.
